title: Senior's toolkit: driving the gateway
summary: Kong's Admin API, decK for config as code, key checks and a quick burst test for rate limits.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: driving the gateway
body: Kong is the example here; Azure API Management, Apigee and AWS API Gateway have the same ideas behind their own CLIs.
The Admin API (port 8001) changes the gateway; the proxy (port 8000) is what clients call. The Admin API must never be reachable from outside.

toolkit.what: Reads what the gateway is really running: which upstreams, which paths, which plugins with which config. Faster than clicking through a console.
flags: paths and hosts that map to a service
auth, rate limiting and the rest, with config

toolkit.what: Creates a service and a route, which is all it takes to publish an upstream through the gateway.
flags: a service pointing at the backend
toolkit.example: curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8001/services --data name=orders --data url=http://orders:8080 && curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8001/services/orders/routes --data 'paths[]=/orders'

toolkit.what: Turns on a policy for one service, such as key authentication or a rate limit.
Creates an API consumer's key. Keys belong to consumers, so limits and logs are per application.
flags: issue a key (Kong generates one if you send none)
toolkit.example: curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8001/consumers --data username=shop-web && curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8001/consumers/shop-web/key-auth | jq -r .key

toolkit.what: decK keeps the gateway's whole config in a YAML file in Git. `diff` shows what would change, `sync` applies it. This is how teams avoid hand-made Admin API changes in production.
flags: show what a sync would change
make the gateway match the file
only touch entities with that tag
toolkit.example: deck gateway diff kong.yaml --select-tag team-orders && deck gateway sync kong.yaml --select-tag team-orders
toolkit.when: every gateway change after the first experiment

toolkit.what: Generates Kong services and routes from an OpenAPI contract, so the gateway config follows the contract instead of being typed twice.
Fires a burst of requests to see a rate limit or a 429 for yourself, and prints a summary of the status codes.

steps.prompt: Match each call to what it does.
pairs: list every policy the gateway applies
map a path to the orders upstream
issue an API key to an application
preview how the gateway would change

prompt: A partner says every call returns `429` since this morning. You run:
Their contract allows 600 a minute. What do you check next?
options: `curl :8001/plugins | jq` to see which rate-limiting plugin with `minute: 5` applies to their consumer or the service
Restart the gateway to clear the counters
Ask the partner to add retries
steps.explain: The headers say a limit of 5 per minute is in force, which matches no contract. Someone set or scoped a plugin wrongly (a test value, or a global plugin). Find it in `/plugins`, fix it in the decK file, and `deck gateway sync`.

steps.prompt: Preview, then apply, the gateway config from Git, touching only your team's entities.
steps.explain: `diff` shows the changes; `sync` makes the gateway match the file, including deletions of tagged entities not in the file. `dump` goes the other way, from the gateway to a file.

items: List the plugins on the orders service
Issue a key for a new consumer
Check which response headers a partner really gets
`deck gateway sync` the config from Git

steps.prompt: A colleague fixed a route in production with `curl -X PATCH :8001/routes/...` during an incident. Next week's `deck gateway sync` undid the fix. What is the lasting lesson?
options: Put the fix in the decK file in Git as well; a sync makes the gateway match the file, so manual changes are temporary
Run `deck gateway dump` before every sync and commit nothing
Use the Admin API for all changes
steps.explain: With config as code, the file is the truth. An emergency change through the Admin API is fine, as long as the same change lands in Git right after; `deck gateway diff` would have shown the drift before the sync.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Read the gateway's real config with the Admin API before you guess, and change it through the decK file in Git with a `diff` first. When a partner reports 401 or 429, reproduce it with their key and `curl -D -`, and read the headers.
